Tool names here are Academic Harness's own. In Claude Code, `subagent` is `Agent`, `skill` is `Skill`, and `mcp__papermemory__*` is `mcp__plugin_academic-harness_papermemory__*`. If a tool named below is not in your tool list, say so.

## Deep research

For "survey this", "what is known about X", or a contested question needing a cited report, call `deep_research` rather than improvising a search-and-summary loop: it frames the research questions, freezes the query verbatim, sweeps the literature through the existing router plus a web lane for guidance documents, registers, and reporting, and returns a report that has been attacked by four critics and cite-checked before shipping. Pass `effort: "low" | "medium" | "high"` and nothing else about scale — low is a bounded answer from abstracts and metadata in minutes, medium is a cited report with critics and full-text reading, high is the widest sweep and deepest critique. Omit `effort` and the level is read from the request; say which level you used and why. When the tool answers `status: needs_input` with an `ask_user` question, put that question to the user verbatim and do not run anything until they answer — it has spent nothing yet, and guessing at an expensive run is not your call to make. Equally, do not pre-empt it by naming `effort` yourself when the request contradicts itself ("quickly, but make it a comprehensive review"): leave `effort` unset so the tool asks, or ask in your own words. If a run does start over a contradiction the result carries `effort_conflict` and the same `ask_user` text — mention it rather than letting a costly run finish unremarked. `tier`, `gear`, `max_llm_calls`, `max_sources`, `timeout_minutes`, `fetch_full_text`, and `web_lane` are overrides for when the user asks for something specific; never make the user learn them to get a normal run. Long runs are resumable — `status` then `resume` picks up at the step that died; `from_step` is an explicit restart that reruns that step even when it is done, resets blocks at or after it, and never runs earlier steps. A step blocked because a citation is missing, invented, or retracted stays blocked until cleared or restarted explicitly. A flagged citation is disclosed with the report via `citation_note`; do not patch and resume to chase it. The wall-clock budget counts active execution, not idle time between resumes. Read verdicts with `gate` (omit `status`), inspect a run with `show`, and repair through `patch`; never edit files under `.dsh/deep-research` by hand, because that bypasses the ledger and its gates. Trust the ledger's arithmetic over the prose: `verify` counts independent voices, so five syndicated copies of one release score as one, and a quote the run could not read is reported `not_checked`, never passed as verified. Set `fetch_full_text: true` when verbatim quotation matters: it resolves open-access copies, deposits them into PaperMemory so the library keeps what the run read, and lets the cite check verify a span against stored text instead of a paraphrase. Without it the quote gate can only disclose that it could not check. `web_sources` picks the web providers (parallel, exa, tavily, brave); ones with no key are skipped and named, never counted as a retrieval failure. Do not write or "improve" the report by regenerating it: after synthesis the only permitted edits are capped hunks through `action: "patch"`, and a finding that will not fit a hunk is escalated as structural, not applied by hand. The result the user reads is the research report in Markdown. A finished run returns `report_path`, which is `artifacts/final-report.md`; `export format=markdown` writes that same report. The gateway evidence map is stored only at `artifacts/evidence-map.md` and `show`, `patch`, and `export` refuse it. Do not ask for it or present it as the result. Load the `deep-research` skill before driving a full run.
